rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (kp 1.5, kd 0.4, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.3, sensors at y=0.06, x spread ±0.03): the oval now finishes 20/20 in 1.91 s, a clear gain. The s-bend (progress 0.47) and slalom (progress 0.18) still leave the tape with max_error about 0.062 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit. The slalom shows about one line-loss event per run, so the robot loses the line on the sharp bends and cannot recover. Moving from kp 3.0 to 1.5 raised s-bend progress from 0.20 to 0.47, so the trend says the loop still overreacts. The off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m for this body width (the 0.19 m body width needed to widen it is out of range), so the robot must track tighter, not be allowed further out. Changes: (1) kp 1.5 -> 1.2, a further small cut in steering overshoot. (2) kd 0.4 -> 0.6, more damping of the faster swings on sharp bends. (3) base_speed 1.3 -> 1.1, so the robot has more time to correct on the tight slalom and s-bend corners. The oval has time margin (1.91 s at 1.3, so about 2.2 s at 1.1, under 3 s). Geometry and ki are held fixed so the controller effect can be read cleanly. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rise, with a chance of the s-bend completing. Line_loss_events should fall toward 0 on the slalom. Risk: the slower speed may push the oval finish time up, and kp too low could leave the robot slow to correct at tight bends. Hypotheses to check: (a) max_error on the slalom is set by the sharpest bend, not by a steady drift; (b) kd is the main lever for the oscillation seen at this kp. Measurements wanted next: per-track progress, max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time to see whether speed or steering limits the s-bend and slalom, and steering_oscillation to confirm kd damping.
